TS0450001.message: Expression {expr} could not be evaluated for a row: {detail}.
TS0450001.solution: Check the expression against the fields and types the row actually carries at runtime.

TS0450002.message: The js transform script could not be compiled: {detail}.
TS0450002.solution: Fix the script so it parses as valid JavaScript.

TS0450003.message: The js transform cannot expose exact decimal {value} as a JavaScript number without changing it to zero or infinity.
TS0450003.solution: Use a value whose conversion to a JavaScript number stays finite and does not underflow to zero, or keep this value outside the js transform.

TS0450004.message: The js transform script defines no process(record, ctx) function.
TS0450004.solution: Add a process(record, ctx) function; it is the required entry point of a js transform.

TS0450005.message: The js transform script raised an error while processing a row: {detail}.
TS0450005.solution: Fix the script so it does not throw for this input, or guard the failing operation.

TS0450006.message: The js transform script produced output that is not a valid record: {detail}.
TS0450006.solution: Ensure process returns a record (or emits one) whose before, after and schema are objects or null.

TS0450007.message: Expanding `{path}` needs the row that an update or a delete replaces, but {detail}, so the rows that row produced cannot be removed.
TS0450007.solution: Configure the source to send the whole earlier row: a document store needs change-stream pre-images turned on for the collection, and a relational source needs its replica identity set to full. Sending only the key columns is not enough here.

TS0450008.message: Two elements of one row expanded `{path}` onto the same key {key}, so the target keeps whichever was written last and the other is lost.
TS0450008.solution: Give the elements something that differs between them - a field of their own named by element_key, or their position in the list via include_array_index - or stop the source producing two elements with one identity.
